races.name: Betfred Champagne Trial EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Betfred St Leger Trial Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: According To Mark
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's runner has placed twice over 10f on good ground in similar conditions but steps up to 1m4f for the first time — the trip is an unknown, and finishing fourth on their most recent start suggests they sit just below the class level of the top-rated runners here.

runners_data.name: Brave Hunter
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott rides a horse who has shown a tendency to race prominently and has placed at 12f on good ground, making the step up in trip here at least credible; the T14 strike rate of 0/5 for the yard is a mild negative, and the hg:p headgear flag is worth noting as it has been retained throughout recent form.

runners_data.name: Hatteen
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up operator has twice finished second over 10f on good ground and shapes as a genuine stayer stepping to 1m4f, but 55 days off is a consideration; P J McDonald takes the ride and the horse will need the pace to lift in the straight to deliver their finish.

runners_data.name: Count Bezukhov
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's Irish raider holds an OR of 120 and is the only runner here with a win already on the board over 10f on good going — the step to 1m4f looks like a natural progression; Billy Loughnane has ridden this horse to both career starts and the close partnership is an asset, with a T14 rate of 10/60 confirming the yard is in decent current form.

runners_data.name: Shoof Baeed
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's front-runner won over 10f on good ground on debut and looks likely to lead from the off here; the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.90 is attached because the horse is mapped as prominent rather than as a controlling leader, meaning if a contested pace emerges they may not dominate as comfortably — but with no natural rivals for the front, that risk appears minimal today.

runners_data.name: Poker
runners_data.note: K R Burke's hold-up type has placed over 12f on good ground and twice shown ability from the rear, but the sim-going record of just 1 placing in 4 comparable conditions does not inspire; David Egan will need a honest gallop to deliver them from off the pace, and on current evidence they rate below the top-rated trio on class.

runners_data.name: Saifo
runners_data.note: David Simcock's runner is entirely unexposed — no form string, no going record, and no days-since-last-run figure are available, making this the biggest unknown in the race; Sean Levey is a competent jockey for an unexposed type, but structural analysis cannot assign meaningful probability without evidence.

runners_data.name: Sea And Sun
runners_data.note: The second Charlie Johnston runner has placed in both career starts, including over 12f on good ground, and the step to 1m4f looks a logical progression for a horse bred to stay; lightly raced and with an OR of 120, Sea And Sun represents genuine each-way interest if they improve again, though finishing second twice suggests a tendency to find one too good.

races.paceDynamic: Shoof Baeed is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice over 1m4f on good-to-firm going at Doncaster, and with no genuine rival to press them, Connor Beasley can dictate a controlled, even tempo from the front without burning reserves. Count Bezukhov and Brave Hunter are both prominent-style horses who will likely track Shoof Baeed through the early and middle stages, creating a compact lead group rather than any scrimmage for position. Behind them, Hatteen and Poker will settle further back as genuine hold-up types, dependent on a meaningful pace injection in the home straight to close the gap — on a flat track with a lone, unbothered leader, that injection may never come. This race shape strongly favours prominent, on-pace runners who can sit just off Shoof Baeed and produce a sustained finish, rewarding those with the class and stamina to hit the front inside the final two furlongs rather than closers waiting for a contested pace that will not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Shoof Baeed bowls along unchallenged at a sustainable gallop and the prominent horses cannot quicken past in the straight.
scenarios.body: Shoof Baeed sets a measured pace on the Doncaster straight, and the lack of pressure means the race is run entirely to their advantage through the final quarter-mile; Count Bezukhov, with the highest OR and a win already on good ground over 10f, is the most likely challenger if they can pick off the leader inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Count Bezukhov or Sea And Sun track Shoof Baeed closely and produce superior class to collar them in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: The steady pace suits horses sitting second or third as they conserve energy, then exploit class superiority when asked to quicken on the good-to-firm Doncaster turf; Count Bezukhov's OR of 120 and prior winning form on good ground makes them the standout beneficiary of this shape, with Sea And Sun a second string for the Johnston yard.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front group ties up in the straight, allowing hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: Hatteen has twice finished second over 10f on good ground and has the profile to benefit from any pace collapse, while Poker has shown ability to close from rear when the gallop has been genuine; however, with only one front-runner in the race, this scenario requires an unlikely pace scenario and carries correspondingly low weight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Wildcard Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Saifo, unraced in the data provided, produces an unexposed performance to defeat more exposed rivals.
scenarios.body: David Simcock's unexposed runner carries real uncertainty — no form string and no going data make this an outlier scenario entirely dependent on unknown ability; the price may be generous if Saifo holds Classic-level potential, but the absence of any evidence limits how much structural weight this scenario can carry.

watchPoints.text: Count Bezukhov is the classiest exposed runner in the field and Billy Loughnane will look to track Shoof Baeed closely — if the Irish raider lands in the pocket just off the leader, watch for a decisive move two furlongs out that could settle the race before the hold-up horses engage.

Saifo is entirely unexposed and Sean Levey may have been booked precisely because David Simcock expects a significant performance — monitor the market move pre-race as any substantial shortening from a big price would carry informational weight.

Shoof Baeed's STYLE_FIT flag means Charlie Johnston's team may not position them as aggressively as their natural front-running style demands — if they are restrained early by Count Bezukhov or Sea And Sun pressing them, the controlled gallop they depend on could be compromised.

Hatteen has been off 55 days for Andrew Balding, a yard with a strong record returning horses fresh — if the hold-up horse is fit to peak, the step to 1m4f should unlock more stamina than shown at 10f, but they need the race to be run at a genuinely strong pace to close late on this flat track.

Brave Hunter's headgear flag (hg:p) has been present throughout recent form and the horse has placed over 12f on good ground before — if the pace is steady enough to allow them to race on the front end without burning out, they could outrun their OR-80 rating at a longer price.

races.name: Betfred Supports Jack Berry House Handicap

runners_data.name: Lordsbridge Grey
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Stuart Woods with Robert Havlin aboard; no wins or placings in seven runs on similar going and recent form figures of 63-775 suggest little improvement is imminent, with the trip at 1m6½f two furlongs longer than any of his last five starts raising a genuine stamina question.

runners_data.name: Golden Flame
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with solid form at this trip including a recent win over 16f on good ground, but his natural hold-up style is squeezed further back than ideal by this race's shape; Zoe Lewis claims 7lb which helps on the weights, and his four-from-fifteen record on comparable going shows he can be competitive when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Twilight Safari
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's four-year-old has placed three times over 16-17f in good and good-to-firm ground, giving him the most relevant trip and going profile in the field; Aiden Brookes takes the ride and the trainer has had one winner from eight in the last 14 days, suggesting the yard is ticking over; tracking Tazaman from close range is his best tactical option.

runners_data.name: Tazaman
runners_data.note: The lone front runner in the race for Kevin and Lauren Frost, Joanna Mason takes the ride on a nine-year-old who has placed six times from fifteen runs on good ground including two wins; controlling an uncontested lead over 1m6½f flat suits her style entirely, though the style-fit flag reflects she is operating at the top of her positional comfort zone in a small field.

runners_data.name: Nanny Park
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's four-year-old has shown promise with two third-place finishes from fifteen good-ground runs but has not won; Billy Loughnane is a high-profile booking for a yard with a modest recent strike rate, and the horse's true hold-up racing style is pushed even further from the sharp end by this race's pace structure, making it hard to see how she gets involved.

races.paceDynamic: Tazaman is the sole confirmed front runner in a five-horse field and, unchallenged for the lead, will control tempo from the outset over this 1m6½f trip on good-to-firm ground at Doncaster. With no rival likely to press Tazaman early, she will set a measured, sustainable gallop that keeps the race well within her own terms for as long as possible. The three hold-up types — Lordsbridge Grey, Golden Flame, and Twilight Safari — will be forced to chase from a distance, relying on a strong enough gallop to bring their finishing kicks into play, which a solo front runner dictating pace is unlikely to provide. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: Tazaman controlling an uncontested lead is the dominant tactical reality, and true hold-up horses face an uphill task if the tempo is too conservative to generate momentum from the rear. Note that Golden Flame and Nanny Park are natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the pace map because there are more hold-up types than the map can represent at the rear; Tazaman and, to a lesser extent, Twilight Safari (should she track closer than usual) are best placed to take advantage of the race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tazaman Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tazaman bowls along at a controlled pace and is never seriously headed, dictating from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Tazaman exploits the absence of any pressing rival to set a comfortable gallop and simply keeps tabs on her pursuers, finding enough to hold on as the hold-up horses struggle to close the gap over the final two furlongs. This scenario suits a horse able to race prominently and maintain rhythm; the lone pace-setter on good-to-firm ground over a flat mile-and-six is in an enviable tactical position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tazaman sets a genuinely strong enough gallop that tires her out inside the final furlong, allowing closers to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Golden Flame or Lordsbridge Grey, tracking from midfield, would need a strong pace to have been set to bring their finishing effort into play over the full trip. Both are redistibuted or true hold-up types whose chance depends on race conditions that this particular shape is unlikely to generate, making this scenario a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuine enough mid-race to string the field out and allow a prominent tracking run from Twilight Safari to land at the business end.
scenarios.body: Twilight Safari has placed three times over comparable distances in good ground and could track Tazaman closer than her hold-up tag suggests if positioned handily from the outset. A fast-run race suits her stamina profile and her Doncaster flat-track form is encouraging, giving her a slender each-way chance if the fractions are honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the race bunches in the final two furlongs and devolves into a sprint finish for all five runners.
scenarios.body: A dawdle-then-sprint scenario over 1m6½f is relatively uncommon but possible with only five runners and one pace setter happy to coast. In this case the horse with the best turn of foot on good-to-firm ground wins, and any of the younger hold-up types with speed could theoretically land the spoils, though none have strong credentials for a finish of this nature.

watchPoints.text: Tazaman gets a completely uncontested lead — if Joanna Mason is allowed to bowl along entirely unchallenged, the horse could steal enough margin in the early-to-middle stages to prove very hard to reel in over 1m6½f.

Golden Flame's recent 16f win on good ground is the standout form in the race but his hold-up style is at odds with a slowly-run scenario; watch whether Zoe Lewis tries to ride him closer than usual to compensate for the likely lack of pace.

Twilight Safari is the most likely beneficiary if she tracks Tazaman from the outset rather than settling into her usual rearward position — watch her early positioning as it will define her chance entirely.

The field of only five on a flat Doncaster galloping track could produce a very compressed pace if Tazaman elects to coast — a falsely-run race over this trip would be unusual but the small field size makes it worth monitoring the early sectionals.

Lordsbridge Grey has never raced beyond 10f in his last five starts; the step to 1m6½f is uncharted territory stamina-wise and his ability to see out the trip in a race likely to lack strong pace is a genuine unknown.

races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Big Eagle
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with Warren Greatrex, 66 days off the track and returning at a longer trip of 1m2f than his recent 8f runs; his lone win came when handily placed but the sim-going record reads 0W0P, suggesting he needs things to fall perfectly from the rear.

runners_data.name: Suddenly I See
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard in strong form (9/67 over 14 days) and Connor Beasley retains the ride; won twice at 8f on good ground and steps up in trip having finished fourth on most recent start, but the sim-going profile of 2W3P is encouraging and a prominent position suits.

runners_data.name: Room Fourteen
runners_data.note: Loughnane takes over on a horse with two wins from three starts at 10f on good ground, making the trip and conditions ideally suited; headgear noted (h) and a Fanshawe yard that has been active (7/28 T14), with 2W3P on similar going arguing well for his chances from a prominent pitch.

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who dictates here by default, but recent form reads 26-825 and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that he is not at his most dangerous when he cannot settle in his preferred position — his lead role is uncontested, which is his best chance, yet the overall form is patchy.

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Appleby's runner carries a visor (v) and arrives 13 days after his last outing; he is a genuine hold-up type whose natural race-position is further back than the map shows, redistributed to midfield because there are simply too many closers in this field — his 1W3P on similar going and consistent placing at 8f suggest he stays well enough, though the step to 1m2f at a course that stretches finishers is a question.

runners_data.name: Domination
runners_data.note: Bethell has no runners in the 14-day window so trainer form is unknown; a genuine front-runner by nature who has been mapped into midfield because the prominent slots are full — if he cannot secure his natural prominent position, his chance weakens markedly, though his 10f winning form on good ground is the form line to beat if he fires.

runners_data.name: Island Bear
runners_data.note: Rowan Scott aboard a Newland & Insole-trained three-year-old with 33 days between runs; all recent form is at 7-8f on soft or heavy, making both the trip extension to 1m2f and the good-to-firm ground unproven — the 0W2P sim-going record underlines that uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground but has since run three successive poor efforts; mapped to midfield rather than prominent because the field is too pace-rich for him to find his natural berth, which is a significant disadvantage, and an OR of 71 — the lowest in the field — makes competitive appeal slim.

races.paceDynamic: Obito is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, honest gallop on good-to-firm ground over 1m2f at Doncaster — a track that rewards those who can travel smoothly and quicken off a sustainable tempo. Suddenly I See and Room Fourteen are the natural prominent types most likely to flank Obito in the early stages and press for the early positions behind the leader, giving the race a conventional shape with a settled order from flagfall. The field contains more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate: Domination and Brighton View both want to race prominently but are mapped to midfield because Obito, Suddenly I See, and Room Fourteen are likely to soak up those berths — both are at a style disadvantage and should be discounted accordingly. With a single front-runner setting a measured pace into a long Doncaster straight, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in the first two or three, as genuine hold-up horses may find the tempo insufficient to generate the late surge they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Obito leads as expected and Suddenly I See or Room Fourteen settle in close pursuit, drawing on their form at the trip on similar ground.
scenarios.body: Obito sets a fair gallop and the prominent pair travel within a length or two throughout, with the winner emerging from that small group as they straighten up and use the long Doncaster run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Bridge Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the front group never accelerate far enough to be caught by the rearward runners.
scenarios.body: Big Eagle and Island Bear work through from off the pace but find the leaders have banked enough ground through an uncontested opening mile to hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Domination Forces The Issue
scenarios.trigger: If Domination ignores his mapped position and pushes forward early to challenge Obito for the lead, quickening the tempo.
scenarios.body: A faster pace benefits a runner who can respond to an injection of speed mid-race rather than needing a late sprint, and Domination's recent course-and-distance win shows he handles the track when allowed to race prominently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Swooper Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a genuine change of pace in the final two furlongs catches the prominent horses flat-footed on a day when the ground rides quicker than expected.
scenarios.body: A faster surface rewards horses with a sharp turn of foot over these closers' preferred plodding style, but with no true hold-up specialist in the field this scenario depends on horses racing out of their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Suddenly I See's trainer form (9/67 over 14 days) combined with two wins on good ground at a similar trip makes him one to follow closely if he travels prominently behind Obito — any sign of travelling strongly into the straight is a danger signal.

Domination's redistribution to midfield is the biggest pace complication: watch whether Sean Bowen pushes forward before the first furlong is complete — if he does, the race shape changes materially and the tempo picks up.

Room Fourteen has headgear (hood) fitted and two wins at 10f on good ground; if Billy Loughnane opts to drop him in rather than press forward, the horse may not be racing to his optimum — watch the early positioning closely.

Island Bear carries unproven going and trip flags simultaneously — on ground that has been riding good-to-firm all day, connections should be watched at the start to see whether he is settled or struggles early.

Obito's last five runs at 10f show a mixed sim-going record (12/15 entries, 2W7P) and his weight of 142lbs is the heaviest in the field by some margin — monitor whether he gets first run once the field straightens up or if the weight begins to tell in the final furlong.

races.name: Betfred Nifty 50 Handicap (Rnd)

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old has won and placed multiple times over this exact course and trip on Good ground, making her the standout course-and-distance specialist; her hold-up style means she needs to be produced late but her sim-going record of 1W4P from nine runs is the best in the field.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes the mount on this six-year-old whose recent form reads 3-6-5-3-6 in a tight band — consistent without threatening; she is a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot by the weight of closers in this field, which will likely cost her the prominent early cover she would prefer.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: Charlie Clover's three-year-old was an impressive winner over 7f on Good recently and Billy Loughnane is a bold booking; his natural closer's instinct places him deep in the field, displaced from the rear by the overcrowded hold-up contingent, and the step up to a mile on this going requires a leap of faith.

runners_data.name: Okiru
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's three-year-old is the race's only genuine front-runner and will secure an uncontested lead; his form figures of 5-6-U-5-7 are modest but the ability to control tempo on a flat, right-handed track without a single rival wanting to press him is a significant tactical advantage that his bare form does not reflect.

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.note: David Egan rides this lightly-raced three-year-old who has only four runs to his name and has yet to win; his best effort was a third over 7f on Good at the start of his career, and the step to a mile represents an open question, though Egan's ability to place a horse just off the pace could see him involved late.

runners_data.name: Myrrh
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old has placed twice from seven runs on similar ground and his jockey Daniel Tudhope is a strong booking on a course Tudhope knows well; he is a genuine hold-up performer shuffled into a midfield spot on the map due to overcrowding at the rear, and his recent runs have been over longer trips where the slower pace suits a horse that takes time to warm up.

runners_data.name: The Anthony Gover
runners_data.note: Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole's three-year-old goes in headgear and has 34 days between runs, which is worth noting for a horse with no wins and no places on Good going from five attempts; he is a natural closer squeezed forward on the map by the density of hold-up types, and his record on similar ground — zero wins or places from five — gives little encouragement even if he finds daylight.

races.paceDynamic: Okiru is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no rival likely to push hard for the lead, will be gifted a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground around Doncaster's sweeping mile. The pace will be honest but controlled — Okiru dictating tempo without being harassed — which compresses the finish and shortens the time available for hold-up horses to reel in the leader from the rear. The bulk of this field — Kiss Me My Love, Princess Niyla, Norcross Brow, Celtic Chariot, Myrrh, and The Anthony Gover — are all natural hold-up or prominent types, meaning the midfield will be congested and several will be racing out of their preferred position. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently just behind Okiru and produce a clean sustained run through the final two furlongs, rather than the true closers who will be caught in traffic with limited time to accelerate. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate naturally; of those, Princess Niyla, Myrrh, and The Anthony Gover are most likely to be shuffled furthest back and unable to secure their preferred spot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Okiru Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Okiru bowls along uncontested and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in the short Doncaster straight.
scenarios.body: Okiru sets a metronomic, untroubled pace and the compressed finish gives the closers insufficient time to reel him in; the Good to Firm surface and flat track suit a horse in command of its own rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking type settles just off Okiru's pace and produces a clean run to overhaul the leader inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Kiss Me My Love has shown the ability to track and finish strongly at this trip on similar ground, and a well-positioned horse two lengths off the pace entering the straight can simply outstay the front-runner as the tempo eases.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congested Midfield, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the hold-up horses find a run through a tiring mid-pack in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A busier gallop burns up Okiru and the prominently-placed horses, opening a gap for a hold-up type to finish through late; Norcross Brow's recent winning form and Billy Loughnane's ability to find space make this the most credible late-closer scenario despite the redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Okiru runs too freely, the field concertinas at the two-furlong pole, and an unexposed runner finds clear daylight at a big price.
scenarios.body: The Anthony Gover's form has been consistent in defeat and, given an unimpeded passage, the headgear runner could outrun his odds in a chaotic finish; however, his redistribution to midfield and zero wins from five similar-going starts make this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Okiru (Vigors) — watch whether he bowls clear unchallenged in the first two furlongs; if he gets a soft lead unchallenged, he becomes significantly harder to catch on this flat track.

Kiss Me My Love (Mason) — watch her position exiting the bend; if she can track in fourth or fifth without being blocked by the congested hold-up pack, her course-and-distance form puts her in the mix late.

Celtic Chariot (Egan) — David Egan is known for positioning horses just off a lone front-runner; watch for him to slot in second or third early, as that is the most dangerous tactical move in this field.

Norcross Brow (Loughnane) — recent winner in the field but racing out of natural position here; watch whether Loughnane commits to tracking or accepts the rear, as that choice will determine whether the mile trip plays to his strengths.

Myrrh (Tudhope) — Tudhope may try to creep into a better position than the horse's natural style dictates; watch for him to be closer than expected at halfway, which would suggest O'Meara has specifically prepared him for a more prominent ride today.

races.name: Betfred Play Fred's 5 Million Pound Handicap

runners_data.name: King's School
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has won and placed at exactly this 7f trip, most recently winning over 7f on soft-to-firm at Thirsk — the step to Good To Firm poses no concern; trained by Gemma Tutty whose 14-day strike rate is quiet (0/14), and 27 days between runs is routine for this type.|

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's stable is in form (1/6 over 14 days) and this horse has strong recent course-relevant history, winning over 7f on Good — as the lone front-runner on fast ground he sets the race's tempo and any free passage to the lead makes him hard to dislodge until the very end.|

runners_data.name: Monsieur Bondy
runners_data.note: Won two of his last five at this exact 7f trip on comparable going, but the two most recent runs show back-to-back 10th-place finishes — form is a significant concern and Geoff Oldroyd's stable is quiet (0/2), though PJ McDonald's presence is a positive tactical factor.|

runners_data.name: Lord Capulet
runners_data.note: Has won and placed multiple times over 7f in varied conditions including Good and Standard, and Kevin Ryan's yard is in strong form (4/33 over 14 days); Toby Moore's 7lb claim is a useful weight relief for a horse whose profile ideally suits racing prominently in a controlled-pace contest.|

runners_data.name: Stanage
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners a horse who has been consistently mid-to-rear in recent outings, finishing no better than 4th in five starts — the move from 8f back to 7f matches his best historical form but top-speed figures are modest and the trainer Easterby yard's recent output (5/41) is moderate.|

runners_data.name: Lope El Fuego
runners_data.note: All five recent runs are on Good ground making the going no concern, and he has a win over 6f on Good — dropping back from 7f to shorter in recent starts suggests 7f may be on the stretch, though the hold-up profile could suit if a stronger pace develops than Alpha Capture is likely to set.|

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good at Redcar and is clearly effective on this surface and trip, but her natural front-running preference cannot be fully expressed today with Alpha Capture already holding that slot — the style-fit discount (0.93) is real, and Scott Dixon's yard is in modest recent form (1/19).|

runners_data.name: Wrydcroft
runners_data.note: Three wins and three places over 7f on Good and Standard underline strong course-type suitability, and the Pam Sly stable is in excellent short-term form (1/2); however, being a genuine prominent racer who has been pushed back into a midfield position by the race shape means he will need to overcome his displaced role to threaten.|

runners_data.name: Return Of The Gods
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's yard is in solid form (4/32) and Billy Loughnane is a top-level booking — this 3yo has placed at 6f on Good but steps up in trip today, and his one attempt at 6f produced a third so the 7f distance is an open question rather than a confirmed asset.|

runners_data.name: Highland Shah
runners_data.note: Won over exactly 7f on Good on his most recent start making going and trip both confirmed positives, but Julie Camacho has mapped him as a headgear horse and he is a front-end racer who genuinely cannot get to the position he needs here — the style displacement (0.90 fit) is the biggest question mark against him.|

races.paceDynamic: Alpha Capture is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should slot onto a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the gate — Good To Firm conditions at Doncaster will ensure the pace is honest but controlled rather than suicidal. Behind him, Lord Capulet, Monsieur Bondy and Return Of The Gods will press from the prominent positions, creating a compact early order that is unlikely to string the field out dramatically. Critically, this field contains more genuine prominent-racing types than the race shape can accommodate: Bella Bisbee, Wrydcroft and Highland Shah are all natural front-end horses who have been mapped to midfield purely because Alpha Capture takes precedence and the prominent slots are already occupied — they will be racing out of their preferred role. This controlled, single-pacemaker shape on fast ground at Doncaster's straight seven favours horses who can race prominently in the first three or four and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — free-going hold-up types are less advantaged when the tempo is metronomic rather than explosive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpha Capture Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha Capture dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the race develops into a sustained-speed test from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Alpha Capture sets fractions that suit horses tracking him in second or third, and the steady tempo means the race is not truly run to suit closers making up ground from the rear. Lord Capulet and Return Of The Gods, both prominent racers with strong form at exactly this trip and going, are ideally placed to challenge off the controlled pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is marginally quicker than expected and the front rank ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: King's Schools hold-up profile becomes an asset if the race is run at a truly strong clip and the closers find themselves with a clear run to pounce late. Stanage and Lope El Fuego, both genuine rear-of-field types on good-to-firm, would also benefit from any significant late fade through the leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Types Overcome Role
scenarios.trigger: If Wrydcroft, Highland Shah or Bella Bisbee manage to secure a closer position to the pace than their mapped placement suggests.
scenarios.body: Should the early breakaway compact unexpectedly and allow these natural front-end horses to slot closer to Alpha Capture than anticipated, their race-fitness and prominent-racing preference becomes relevant again. Wrydcroft in particular has recent course-relevant form and a 3-4 placed profile at this trip on matching going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Tactical Shake-Up
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha Capture fails to stride on or meets interference early, fragmenting the anticipated pace structure entirely.
scenarios.body: Without a reliable pace anchor the race becomes tactical and unpredictable, benefiting horses with flexible racing styles who can respond to a variable tempo. Monsieur Bondy's class on this trip and Return Of The Gods' course profile give them the best chance of capitalising in a messy, unstructured contest.

watchPoints.text: Alpha Capture's ability to lead uncontested is the fulcrum of this race — if he is pressured out of the gate by Lord Capulet or Monsieur Bondy, the controlled tempo assumption breaks down entirely.|

Bella Bisbee, Wrydcroft and Highland Shah are all natural prominent horses who cannot all get that position — watch the first two furlongs to see which of the three actually secures a forward berth and which is forced to cover extra ground settling into midfield.|

Lord Capulet is partnered by a 7lb claimer (Toby Moore) in what is effectively a handicap scenario where the weight relief is real but race-experience in a competitive field at this level is unproven — any signs of greenness in the straight should be noted.|

Good To Firm conditions are confirmed on course (the going report aligns with the 5:05 7f slot) — horses with a record on soft or heavy ground only should be downgraded, and King's School's recent win on soft-to-firm should be considered in context of what may be faster ground today.|

races.name: Betfred Follow Us On X Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Hurt You Never
runners_data.note: Consistent placed record on good ground over 5f (3W5P in similar going) gives strong course-and-going credentials, but naturally races from the rear and in this field with multiple hold-up types is unlikely to find clear space early; at 7, experience may help him weave through.|

runners_data.name: Donald
runners_data.note: Blinkers fitted, which can sharpen early focus, yet his form reads as a hold-up horse who finds positions 2nd-5th from behind the pace; over 5f on good ground here, getting shuffled to a midfield berth rather than his natural rearward slot is a slight ask.|

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted and tends to race at the back of the field naturally, but consistent 5-8th finishes over 6f on good ground suggest a horse who rarely lands a serious blow; being funnelled into midfield on a flat sprint track does little to improve those prospects.|

runners_data.name: Koffee And Kale
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on soft and placed over 6f on good, so handles varying conditions; cheekpieces fitted to aid concentration, and if she can sit handy off the pace, her finishing effort over this trip makes her one of the more plausible hold-up-profile threats in this specific field.|

runners_data.name: Bayraat
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who has hit remarkable recent form — 1st, 2nd, 2nd from three recent runs over 6f on good — and is genuinely prominent by nature; likely to press Dicko The Legend for position and should get to race in his optimal front-rank spot without fighting for it.|

runners_data.name: Mister Moet
runners_data.note: Has shown form on standard going but all recent runs have come on all-weather at Southwell and Wolverhampton, making this turf assignment on good-to-firm an open question; 97 days off adds another layer of risk for this 3yo in amateur company.|

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Sir
runners_data.note: Won a 6f race on good ground just 10 days ago, giving him a sharp fitness edge; naturally a hold-up horse but has placed form from just off the pace, and if he can track into a prominent position rather than his habitual rear berth, his recent form makes him one of the more interesting unexposed runners.|

runners_data.name: Powernap
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 5f and 6f on good ground recently and wears a tongue-tie, showing improving profile for trainer Jessica Bedi; a genuine come-from-behind type who will need gaps to appear on this flat track, but her form trajectory over this trip is trending in the right direction.|

runners_data.name: Saucy Jane
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 70 and has two wins over 6f on good ground, most recently last time out; naturally holds up but has winning form, and if she can sit midfield in a race with a controlled pace rather than a frenetic one, her class gives her a strong late argument.|

runners_data.name: Dicko The Legend
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and the only genuine pace-setter in this field, which gives him total control of the tempo over this flat 5½f; STYLE_FIT flag reflects that the map role as sole leader in a large field is slightly outside his comfort zone, but with no rival to press him, the conditions are as good as they get for his style.|

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: Four consecutive top-four finishes over 5f and 5f on good and standard going for the powerful Tim Easterby yard (15 winners from 90 in 14 days); most consistent runner in the field on this surface, last run just 7 days ago keeps him sharp, and his ability to travel prominently suits a race where the lead is likely to be sustainable.|

races.paceDynamic: Dicko The Legend is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 5½f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, should bowl along at a sustainable gallop from the off on good-to-firm ground at Doncaster. Bayraat is prominent by style and will likely press for early position, but the dominant pace narrative belongs to Dicko The Legend setting fractions he controls rather than fights for. With the pace single and uncontested, this race is set up to reward horses who can travel in close pursuit without being committed to a deep hold-up run — prominent racers and horses who can sit just off the leader in the slipstream are the primary beneficiaries, as any late challenge from true closers must cover ground on a flat, straight 5½f track where the lead is rarely surrendered cheaply. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Hurt You Never, Mister Moet, Lieutenant Sir, Powernap and Donald are all genuine come-from-behind horses who are mapped to midfield simply because there is no room for them all at the rear; Dicko The Legend and Bayraat are by far the most likely to secure their natural forward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Lead Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Dicko The Legend bowls clear from the gate and is never seriously pressured, dictating fractions on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Dicko The Legend sets a sustainable pace on his own terms, with Bayraat the only likely company; horses that travel prominently just off the leader can strike at the two-furlong marker before hold-up types find their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominated By Finisher
scenarios.trigger: If Dicko The Legend and Bayraat set a falsely strong gallop and tie each other up, leaving a window for a prominently-placed finisher to reel them in.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Applause, who has consistent placed form over 5f on good ground, is ideally suited to tracking the pace from just off the front two and swooping late; Saucy Jane's recent winning form over 6f on good ground gives her the stamina to finish strongly when others fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Gets Lucky Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the final furlong and a well-timed late run threads through a gap from the rear.
scenarios.body: Koffee And Kale, who has shown ability from off the pace on fast surfaces, could benefit if the race falls apart in front; however, most redistributed hold-up horses here are racing out of their natural position, making this a lower-probability outcome on a flat, unforgiving track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a slow early pace suddenly quickens mid-race and causes a bunching effect through the field.
scenarios.body: Lieutenant Sir showed a smart win over 6f on good ground last time and, if the race turns tactical and chaotic, could produce a burst from a midfield position; this shape is the least likely given the straightforward 5½f layout and a front-runner who has every reason to stride on.

watchPoints.text: Bayraat's recent 1-2-2 form over 6f on good ground makes him the most dangerous challenger to Dicko The Legend for early supremacy — watch whether he pushes up to dispute the lead or settles just behind, as that choice shapes the entire race.

Spirit Of Applause has posted four consecutive places over 5f on good and standard going and arrives in sharp form (7 days since last run); if he gets a clean passage tracking the pace, his consistency makes him a serious danger at the business end.

Saucy Jane is the top-rated runner (OR 70) and has two wins over 6f on good ground — if the pace is comfortable and she can travel smoothly from midfield, her class could overhaul the front pair in the final furlong.

Several genuine hold-up horses (Hurt You Never, Mister Moet, Lieutenant Sir, Powernap) are all mapping to midfield positions they do not naturally occupy — watch the first furlong for any of them being forced wide or losing lengths as they seek space that does not naturally exist in this race shape.

Mister Moet has not run for 97 days and all recent form comes on all-weather surfaces — watch for any signs of ring-rustiness or inability to handle good-to-firm turf, which would effectively remove him from contention before the race reaches its conclusion.
